records.name: Philly Track Jawn
records.summary: A community running group in Philadelphia that trains on the track on Tuesday evenings and holds weekend runs and walks. Certified coaches lead the workouts, and people of all fitness levels are welcome.
records.what_you_do: Join a Tuesday evening track workout at the Temple University Sports Complex, or sign up for the weekend runs and walks. Fill out the group's sign-up form first.

schedule.text: Tuesdays at 7 pm for track workouts at the Temple University Sports Complex. Weekend runs and walks have no set time listed on the site.

locations.label: Temple University Sports Complex (Tuesday track workouts)

cost.text: Tuesday track workouts are free. The site does not say whether the weekend runs and walks cost anything.

first_step.how: Fill out the group's sign-up form on its website, then come to a Tuesday track workout
first_step.basis: The site says people of all fitness levels are welcome and gives a sign-up form, so the way in is clear.

records.notes: The April 2025 guide also lists a Thursday 6 pm session, but the group's own site shows only the Tuesday track workout, so Thursday is left out. The site has an updated label with no full date.

records.name: Philly Girls Who Walk
records.summary: A walking group for women in Philadelphia that takes walks of about three miles. The site says everyone is welcome.
records.what_you_do: Pick an upcoming walk from the group's Heylo page and walk with the group. Walks are free.

schedule.text: Walk dates vary. Upcoming walks are posted on the group's Heylo page, and the April 2025 guide describes walks of about three miles.

cost.text: Free, according to the group's website.

first_step.how: Use the Join us link on its website, which goes to the group's Heylo page, then pick an upcoming walk
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome and links to a clear way to join, but it shows no walk times or newcomer program.

records.notes: The group's website has no dated posts and no walk times. The schedule is posted only on its Heylo page, which was not read. Status rests on the April 2025 guide.

records.name: Swagga House Run Club
records.summary: A non-competitive run club that stresses encouragement and friendship. Its website says it serves Black and brown communities and that all levels are welcome, and the April 2025 guide lists a monthly run of 1 to 5 miles.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly group run or walk of 1 to 5 miles. Ask on Instagram or through the contact page on the website where the next run starts.

schedule.text: Monthly group run, usually on a Sunday at 8 am, according to the April 2025 guide. The site does not list dates.

cost.text: No run or membership fee is shown on its website.

first_step.how: Message the group on Instagram or use the contact page on its website to ask about the next run
first_step.basis: The site says all levels are welcome but does not say how to join, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The website has no dated posts. A 2026 date appears only inside an image file name, so it was not used as evidence. The schedule and run length come from the April 2025 guide.

records.name: Nice Jewish Runners Philadelphia
records.summary: A social running and walking group in Philadelphia that meets on Sunday mornings and gathers afterward for a snack and coffee.
records.what_you_do: Run or walk with the group on Sunday mornings, then stay for the social time. Join through the group's Heylo page to see the events.

schedule.text: Sundays at 10 am, according to the April 2025 guide. The meeting place is posted each week.

locations.label: Philadelphia, location posted weekly on the group's page

cost.text: No fee is shown on the group's Heylo page or in the April 2025 guide.

first_step.how: Use the Heylo invite link to join the group and see its events
first_step.basis: The group's page says people join to see all the events, and it shows no fee or newcomer step, so the way in is not clear.

records.notes: The Heylo group page shows about 300 check-ins and no dated events. The group's Instagram was not read. The name includes Jewish, but no page says who may join, so the audience is public and no faith tag is set. The Sunday 10 am time comes from the April 2025 guide, not the Heylo page.

records.name: We Walk PHL
records.summary: A free citywide walking program run by Philadelphia Parks and Recreation, supported by the Fairmount Park Conservancy and the Department of Public Health. Trained community volunteers lead walks of about an hour in city parks.
records.what_you_do: Walk with a group at a park near you and pick the pace that suits you. Walks take place one to three times a week depending on the site, and some groups meet all year.

schedule.text: One to three walks a week at different parks, about an hour each. Times and places are posted on the We Walk PHL Facebook group.

first_step.how: Check the We Walk PHL Facebook group for this week's walks, then show up at a park. The city page also links a GivePulse registration page.
first_step.basis: Every group has two trained leaders, a slowest-pace group is available, and anyone can drop in.

records.notes: Park names and times change by site, so the Facebook group is the place to check. The city article is dated September 10, 2025, and the PhillyVoice article is dated September 3, 2026. The Fairmount Park Conservancy preseason page had no details and no date, so it is not used. Ages are not stated, so the crowd is all_ages.

records.name: Hunting Park We Walk PHL walkers
records.summary: A walking group in the Hunting Park neighborhood that is part of the citywide We Walk PHL program. Most members are in their 60s to 80s, and the group has slow, medium and fast walks.
records.what_you_do: Walk with the group about three times a week, pick the pace group that suits you, and finish with a cool down. Newcomers can attend a group meetup or accept an invitation from a walker met on the route.

schedule.text: About three times a week, for about 45 minutes plus a cool down. Specific days and start times are not given.

cost.text: Free, through the citywide We Walk PHL program.

first_step.how: Go to a We Walk PHL group meetup, look for the group on Facebook, or accept an invitation from a walker met on the route
first_step.basis: The group has slow, medium and fast walks, and the article describes a newcomer who joined.

records.notes: No own website for this group. Everything here comes from a WHYY article dated October 21, 2025. The group has no published days or start times, and the ages come from the article as approximate. The citywide program is in the We Walk PHL record above.

records.name: PHA senior centers (Wilson Park, Cassie L. Holley, Emlen Arms)
records.summary: Three senior centers on the Philadelphia Housing Authority's website that offer walking classes for older adults. Attending is free, and the page does not show class times.
records.what_you_do: Call to ask which center has walking classes and when they meet, then join a class at the center nearest you.

schedule.text: Walking classes are offered. Days and times are not shown on the PHA page, so call to ask.

cost.text: Free. PHA and the Philadelphia Corporation for Aging cover the cost of the services.

first_step.how: Call 215-684-3959, the contact listed for the senior centers, and ask about walking class times
first_step.basis: Who may attend is listed, but class times and sign-up steps are not shown, so a phone call is the way in.

records.notes: The PHA page carries no date, so there is no dated sign of life. Status is probably_active only because the page is live. Walking class times must be confirmed by phone.

notes:
Searches: all 3 used. Search 1 looked for Philly Track Jawn's own site and found no schedule, so its Google Site came from the April 2025 guide and was fetched instead. Searches 2 and 3 covered walking groups for older adults and surfaced We Walk PHL, the Hunting Park walkers and the PHA senior centers, each checked on its own page. Fetches: 18, including one certificate error and one 403. Fetches were not the limit. The limit is that most leads have only Instagram, Facebook, Meetup or X pages, and the brief bars recording facts from those platforms, so 38 leads stay unchecked in leads_only. Most records here rest on the April 2025 guide, the newest dated evidence for them, so their status is probably_active unless noted. Verdicts: 7 publish, 0 hide.

Dropped: Guy's Racing Club, because its site failed the certificate check and the Bicycle Coalition page gives no cost or way to join. Hike + Heal, because its own site shows no membership or drop-in price and the April 2025 guide lists $350 a year, so it is not low cost. The Endorphins Running Linktree leads only to a global app, so it is not recorded for Philadelphia.

Conflict: the April 2025 guide lists Philly Track Jawn on Thursdays at 6 pm too, but the group's own site lists only the Tuesday track workout. Thursday is left out.

Reading limits: the Billy Penn guide page is about 100,851 characters, and the fetch read the first 100,000, so the last part was not read. The earlier run noted an August 2026 update date on that page; I did not rely on it. The Swagga site shows a 2026 date only inside an image file name, which is not evidence.

Not recorded: a third-party listing (not read) mentions a 2025 Wednesday walk at West Oak Lane Senior Center. The Senior Strut is a one-time annual event, so it is skipped. Outside the city, so skipped: Conshohocken Running Club, Bensalem Girlies, Phoenixville Beer Runners, RUNegades, West Chester groups, Central Bucks Bicycle Club, Delaware Valley Bicycle Club and Team Evesham. Students Run Philly Style and Original Propaganda Athletic Club appear in the guide but outside this slice, and were not checked. Major Taylor Cycling Club of Philadelphia is on the Bicycle Coalition list with its own site, but an earlier run got a 403 on it, and I did not retry.
